SOUTH KOREA ORDAINED THE WORLD'S FIRST ROBOT MONK
slides.body: Gabi became the world's first robot monk at Seoul's Jogye Temple. The 130cm Unitree G1 humanoid wore robes, received a 108-bead rosary, and pledged to respect all life

slides.headline: THIS ISN'T A GIMMICK. IT'S A PATTERN.
slides.body: Robots and AI keep showing up in places nobody predicted — temples, courtrooms, clinics, kitchens. Every "first" like this one starts as a headline and ends as an industry standard. The gap between the two is getting shorter every year

slides.headline: AI IS ALREADY CHEAP ENOUGH FOR NORMAL BUSINESSES
slides.body: The same AI that runs a robot monk answers your emails, sorts your invoices, and writes your reports. The winners aren't the ones who know about AI — they're the ones who put it to work first

slides.body: Daily AI news, tools, and how to actually use them in your business. Follow so you never fall behind

caption:
Swipe 📲 for the biggest AI stories of the last 7 days — from the world's first robot monk to the AI tools quietly landing inside normal businesses.

South Korea ordained Gabi, a 130cm Unitree G1 humanoid, as the world's first robot monk at Seoul's Jogye Temple, robots and AI kept showing up in temples, courtrooms, clinics and kitchens, and the same tech behind the headlines became cheap enough for everyday businesses to put to work on emails, invoices and reports.

Every AI "first" starts as a headline and ends as an industry standard — and the gap between the two gets shorter every year. The winners aren't the ones who know about AI, they're the ones who put it to work first.

Sources: Reuters, Yonhap, Jogye Order, Unitree
